newsitem.title: USA: Rural Cellular sees near-breakeven in '97.
newsitem.headline: Rural Cellular sees near-breakeven in '97.

text.p: Rural Cellular Corp said Monday even though it expects to post significantly improved EBITDA and revenues in 1997, interest expenses are likely to cause the company to record near-breakeven results.

It said the interest expense is related to the debt financing of both Unity Cellular Systems Inc, a pending acquisition from InterCel Inc, and to Wireless Alliance, in which Rural Cellular holds a 51 percent equity stake. Rural Cellular said it has received a firm commitment from a lender for this long-term financing.

For 1996, Rural Cellular, which provides wireless telecommunications services in northern Minnesota and contiguous portions of western Wisconsin and eastern North Dakota, reported earnings of $3.5 million or $0.41 per share, up from $790,000 or $0.13 per share.
Revenues rose to $30.5 million from $20.3 million.

Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization increased 53 percent in 1996 to a consolidated total of $1.03 per share. Excluding the impact of the Wireless Alliance, EBITDA advanced 65 percent in 1996.
Revenues in 1996 rose to $30.5 million from $20.3 million.
President Richard Ekstrand, in a statement, said the company's record 1996 operating results reflect strong customer growth as well as the company's continued adherence to a balanced growth strategy.

Rural Cellular said its monthly customer retention rate declined to 98.7 percent from 99.0 percent at year-end 1995, due in part to a portion of Rural Cellular customers living near Wireless Alliance service areas who migrated to Wireless Alliance.
